set_aside.subject: Create replay after an ordinary record change
set_aside.text: This holds while the record the first create made keeps its values
set_aside.question: Which values must remain unchanged, and what happens when a project or customer is corrected or otherwise changes after the first create but before its retry?
options: The retry still returns the original record because replay identity survives ordinary changes.
The retry is treated as a new create because any value changed.
The retry is refused because the current record no longer matches the original create.
set_aside.default_guess: Keep replay identity across ordinary corrections and return the original record in its current state.

witness.initial: A project exists only because an owner create succeeded, but its answer was lost.
events: The owner finds the project in the catalogue.
The owner corrects its display name, moving its revision.
The owner repeats the original create request.
outcomes: Registry recognizes the replay and returns the corrected existing project.
Registry treats it as a new create and makes a second project, or refuses it because the values differ.
witness.observer: The owner, and consumers that see one versus two project identities.

set_aside.subject: Replay of an anonymised project create with a caller-supplied id
set_aside.text: a create repeated after that is a new create
set_aside.question: When the original create supplied a project id that the anonymised record still keeps, must the retry create a new project, or must it be refused because that id is already held with different content?
options: Create a new project under a newly minted id despite the supplied id.
Reuse the retained id by replacing the anonymised record.
Refuse the retry because the retained id conflicts, as R0-07 requires.
set_aside.default_guess: Refuse the retry because an anonymised project still owns its id and cannot be replaced.

witness.initial: An instance contains a project created with caller-supplied id P; the project is archived and anonymised, so it still keeps P but no longer keeps the create content.
events: The owner repeats the original create request carrying id P.
outcomes: The new R0-36 passage treats it as a new create and returns the new record.
R0-07 treats the retained record as holding the same id with different content and refuses the request without changing anything.
witness.observer: The owner and every consumer resolving project id P.

set_aside.subject: Room-create replay after its project is anonymised
set_aside.text: Erasing a customer or anonymising a project removes everything that would tell a repeat; a create repeated after that is a new create
set_aside.question: Does this rule include a repeated room create whose room was removed by project anonymisation, even though adding any room to that archived/anonymised project must be refused?
options: Treat the retry as a new room create.
Refuse it because the parent project is archived/anonymised.
Limit the new-create rule explicitly to customer creates after customer erasure and project creates after project anonymisation.
set_aside.default_guess: Refuse the room retry because its parent project is archived, and limit the exception to the corresponding customer or project create.

witness.initial: An active project exists and an add-room request succeeds, but its answer is lost.
events: The owner archives and anonymises the project, removing its rooms.
The original add-room request is repeated against that project.
outcomes: The changed R0-36 text says the repeated create is a new create.
The add-room action refuses it because the project remains archived.
witness.observer: The caller repeating the room request.

set_aside.subject: Create replay after whole-project deletion
set_aside.text: Erasing a customer or anonymising a project removes everything that would tell a repeat
set_aside.question: What happens when a project is deleted whole and its original create request is then repeated?
options: Treat it as a new create, as after anonymisation.
Retain replay information outside the deleted record and return or refuse the replay.
Refuse the retry because the former identity was deleted.
set_aside.default_guess: Treat it as a new create because whole deletion removes at least as much replay evidence as anonymisation.

witness.initial: A project create succeeded but its answer was lost.
events: The owner finds the project, archives it and chooses whole-project deletion.
The owner repeats the original create request.
outcomes: Registry treats the request as a new create and returns a new project.
Registry retains replay knowledge outside the deleted record and returns or refuses the request as a replay.
witness.observer: The owner and consumers that receive the resulting project identity.
